I read p.145 and the five Axis* files. weight (L28) is a_{αβ} of (B.4) exactly, and axisSpace_norm_le_iff makes the norm the sup quotient. Every clause has a faithful counterpart: product ≤ 64, J_r ≤ 80, average ≤ 1, mulY ≤ 80, I ≤ 80, ∂_η I ≤ 80/ρ, mixed (B.6) ≤ 5120/ρ, both derivative-omitted variants, and 64 per inserted factor. Lean covers every natural r ≥ 1, any window and explicit constants, so lean_stronger stands, with one caveat: uniqueness of the regular solution is not formalised (routine, unused downstream). All three findings have correct premises and are low; none is a material difference. The verdict and relation were unanimous; the MATHEMATICS skeptic dissented only on whether findings 0 and 2 are material.

findings.summary: No declaration bundles or cites Lemma B.1. Its clauses are proved faithfully in about fifteen declarations across AxisOperators, AxisEvaluationAlgebra and AxisInverseFactors, so the pairing is inferred, not declared.
Lean defines J_ν by the coefficient rows (B.5) and proves that this series is a smooth solution with G(0)=0. The uniqueness implicit in the paper's 'the solution' is not stated anywhere in Lean.
The variant with F replaced by A_X(F) has no dedicated declaration. It is the composite of norm_inverseMixed_le with norm_average_le (≤ 1), and AxisContraction uses exactly that composite.
